newsitem.title: FRANCE: CIC tender could be relaunched - source.
newsitem.headline: CIC tender could be relaunched - source.

text.p: The privatisation tender for French bank CIC could be declared void after the deadline on Monday and a new tender launched which would result in the bank being sold off in parcels to various groups, a source close to the sell-off process said on Friday.
But the Finance ministry made no official comment. "Those who are candidates are supposed to conform with the terms and conditions of sale," a source there said on Friday.
The government has attached a series of terms and conditions which includes a clause allowing for the tender to be declared void and re-run.

Sixty-seven percent of the Credit Commercial et Industriel (CIC) bank, which is owned by state insurer GAN, has been put up for privatisation by trade sale with the closure of the current tender at 1600 GMT on Monday.

French banks Societe Generale, Banque Nationale de Paris (BNP) and the savings bank grouping Caisses d'Epargne are the most frequently cited as contenders in the bidding for CIC, itself a grouping of 11 regional banks.
None of them would declare their stance and the finance ministry source said the names of those in the running would not be revealed.
A decision on the sale should be taken during the month of November, the ministry source said.
The other source close to the sell-off procedure said that some candidates judged the various terms and conditions of sale "too restrictive".
The terms include safeguarding the "original" operational character of the CIC group and respect for its insurance sales relationship with parent company GAN.

CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt said earlier this week it was important to preserve a "group of banks which were decentralised but coordinated with a nationwide coverage and this identity as a regional bank".
Banking analysts have said it was likely that a large commercial bank such as CIC would have to rationalise.
"Any French buyer would have to deal with overlap, even if it was only in Paris where two networks ran the risk of ending up competing," said one analyst.

The insurance ties are also seen as thorny. GAN will keep 26 percent of CIC and has recently signed 10-year exclusivity deals with CIC for distribution of GAN insurance through the bank's network, with penalty clauses for failure to respect the deal.

Moreover, CIC's net asset value on GAN's books is estimated at more than 14 billion -- which if used as a basis for a sale price comes in at around 9.38 billion for the 67 percent of CIC that is up for grabs.
The source close the the sell-off process said that the Caisses d'Epargne would be the only likely candidate for a takeover of the entire CIC grouping.

"But that would be a political decision," said the source, noting that the French banking association (AFB), which represents the commercial banks like Societe Generale and BNP, would at least demand a hefty trade-off in return, such as a change in the status of the Caisses d'Epargne.
Staff at the Caisses staged a one-day strike on Thursday in defence of their alternative savings bank status.
"It's gradually working its way towards the tender being annulled," said the source close to the affair.

Theorising on the scenario that would ensue if the Caisses d'Epargne was out of the running, the source said there was a possibility that two poles could form to bid for parts of CIC -- one centring around Credit Commercial de France (CCF) and the other including Societe Generale, BNP and possibly a foreign bank like Deutsche Bank.

The second bloc would share out, with Societe Generale taking CIC operations in the west of France, BNP laying its hands on Lyonnaise de Banque and CIC-Paris as well as CIAL in Alsace-Lorraine in the north-east going to Deutsche.
